plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating sp3d hybridization in phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5) at the molecular and orbital levels. Panel (a) shows a ball-and-stick model of PCl5 with an orange phosphorus atom at the center covalently bonded to five green chlorine atoms directed toward the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid: two axial Cl atoms situated above and below the central P atom along a vertical axis, and three equatorial Cl atoms arranged symmetrically in the horizontal plane. Panel (b) depicts the five sp3d hybrid orbitals that account for these five bonds, each shown as a large orange lobe radiating from a central black dot representing the phosphorus nucleus, labeled "sp3d," and arranged in the same trigonal bipyramidal pattern with dashed lines connecting the lobe tips to outline the geometry; small back-lobes are omitted for clarity. This figure establishes sp3d hybridization — derived from mixing one 3s, three 3p, and one 3d orbital of phosphorus — as the valence-bond explanation for the five equivalent bonding regions in PCl5 and connects orbital theory directly to the observed trigonal bipyramidal molecular structure.

elements: Panel (a): central orange phosphorus sphere (large, at origin)
Panel (a): two axial green chlorine spheres directly above and below P along the vertical axis
Panel (a): three equatorial green chlorine spheres at 120° spacing in the horizontal plane
Panel (a): five orange cylindrical bond sticks from P to each Cl (two axial, three equatorial)
Panel (a): specular highlights / shaded spheres giving ball-and-stick look
Panel (a) caption label '(a)' below the model
Panel (b): small black dot at origin representing the phosphorus nucleus
Panel (b): five orange teardrop-shaped sp3d hybrid orbital lobes radiating from the dot along the same five trigonal-bipyramidal directions (two axial up/down, three equatorial)
Panel (b): green dashed lines joining the five lobe tips, outlining the trigonal-bipyramidal framework (3 equatorial triangle edges + 6 apex-to-equator edges)
Panel (b): five italic text labels 'sp3d', one beside each lobe (upper-right, upper-left, left, lower-left, right, bottom as in source)
Panel (b) caption label '(b)' below the diagram

interactions.teaches: The five orange lobes of the sp3d hybrid set occupy exactly the same five directions as the five P–Cl bonds, so orbital shape explains the trigonal bipyramidal molecular geometry.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: Each individual sp3d hybrid orbital points at one specific chlorine; clicking a lobe (or a bond) highlights its partner in the other panel and reveals whether it is an axial (180° apart) or equatorial (120° apart) position.
Rotating shows the trigonal bipyramid is not flat: three equatorial directions lie in one plane at 120°, while the two axial directions stand perpendicular to that plane.

demo_steps.title: The molecule: PCl5
demo_steps.narration: A central orange phosphorus atom is bonded to five green chlorines — two axial, above and below, and three equatorial spread at 120° in the horizontal plane.

demo_steps.title: The orbitals: five sp3d hybrids
demo_steps.narration: Mixing one 3s, three 3p and one 3d orbital gives five equivalent sp3d hybrids, each a large lobe pointing outward from the nucleus; dashed lines trace the trigonal bipyramid they define.

demo_steps.title: Matching orbitals to bonds
demo_steps.narration: Superimposing the two panels shows each lobe aiming straight at a chlorine — click any lobe to see which bond it forms and whether that site is axial or equatorial.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: P nucleus at origin; bond length 1.6 units to equatorial Cl and 1.8 units to axial Cl (axial bonds slightly longer, as in real PCl5). Directions: axial = (0,+1,0) and (0,−1,0); equatorial = unit vectors in the XZ plane at 0°, 120°, 240° (i.e. (1,0,0), (−0.5,0,0.866), (−0.5,0,−0.866)). Panel (a): P sphere radius 0.38, orange #E8721C with lighter specular highlight; Cl spheres radius 0.30, green #4CAF3E / #5CB85C; bond cylinders radius 0.09, orange #E8721C, spanning from P surface to Cl center. Panel (b): black nucleus dot radius 0.07 (#000000); each sp3d lobe is a teardrop/egg shape ~1.5 units long and ~0.55 units max width, fat end outward, narrow tip at the nucleus, axis aligned with its bond direction; fill light-orange gradient #F7C15C → #F0A63C with soft edges, semi-transparent (opacity ~0.85). Small back-lobes are omitted. Dashed lines: green #6E9B3A, 2px, dash 0.09/0.07, drawn as the 9 edges of the trigonal bipyramid connecting lobe-tip endpoints (3 equatorial-equatorial edges, 3 top-apex-to-equatorial, 3 bottom-apex-to-equatorial). Labels 'sp³d' in black italic serif, placed just beyond each lobe tip along its outward direction, offset ~0.35 units outward; panel captions '(a)' and '(b)' centered below each figure. Source view is roughly three-quarter: equatorial plane seen edge-on with a slight downward tilt so one equatorial direction points right, one upper-left, one lower-left; axial lobes read as top and bottom.
interactionPlan.notes: Build both panels as two THREE.Group objects sharing the same five direction vectors, so highlighting is index-linked. Lobes: generate a teardrop via LatheGeometry from a profile r(t) = A·sin(πt)·t^0.6 over t∈[0,1] (pinched at nucleus, bulging near tip), then orient with quaternion setFromUnitVectors(+Y, dir); use MeshStandardMaterial with slight transparency and an emissive tint for highlight state. Dashed geometry via LineSegments + LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Labels as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML so the sp³ superscript renders correctly and stays screen-facing during orbit. Click picking via Raycaster against lobe meshes and bond cylinders/Cl spheres; on select, set the matching lobe and the matching bond+Cl to a highlight color (e.g. #FFD24D lobe, #2E7D32 Cl) and dim the rest to ~0.25 opacity. In 'Overlay both' mode render panel (b) lobes translucent on top of the ball-and-stick model in the same coordinate frame rather than side by side. Toggle between (a) and (b) with a short cross-fade rather than an instant swap so the shared directions are visually preserved.

authoredContext:
In a molecule of phosphorus pentachloride, PCl 5 , there are five P–Cl bonds (thus five pairs of valence electrons around the phosphorus atom) directed toward the corners of a trigonal bipyramid. We use the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and one of the 3 d orbitals to form the set of five sp 3 d hybrid orbitals ( ) that are involved in the P–Cl bonds. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d hybridization include the sulfur atom in SF 4 and the chlorine atoms in ClF 3 and in ClF 4 + . (The electrons on fluorine atoms are omitted for clarity.)

(a) The five regions of electron density around phosphorus in PCl 5 require five hybrid sp 3 d orbitals. (b) These orbitals combine to form a trigonal bipyramidal structure with each large lobe of the hybrid orbital pointing at a vertex. As before, there are also small lobes pointing in the opposite direction for each orbital (not shown for clarity).

Two images are shown and labeled “a” and “b.” Image a depicts a ball-and-stick model in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement. Image b depicts the hybrid orbitals in the same arrangement and each is labeled, “s p superscript three d.”

The sulfur atom in sulfur hexafluoride, SF 6 , exhibits sp 3 d 2 hybridization. A molecule of sulfur hexafluoride has six bonding pairs of electrons connecting six fluorine atoms to a single sulfur atom. There are no lone pairs of electrons on the central atom. To bond six fluorine atoms, the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and two of the 3 d orbitals form six equivalent sp 3 d 2 hybrid orbitals, each directed toward a different corner of an octahedron. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d 2 hybridization include the phosphorus atom in PCl 6 − , the iodine atom in the interhalogens IF 6 + , IF 5 , ICl 4 − , IF 4 − and the xenon atom in XeF 4 .

discrepancies: Rendered colors read darker/muddier than the source: the phosphorus and bonds appear brownish-rust rather than the source's bright orange, and the chlorines are a deep forest green instead of the source's vivid medium green.

The source presents (a) and (b) side by side for direct comparison; the generated figure shows only one panel at a time (toggle/overlay), so the at-a-glance two-panel composition of the original is lost.

In the default (a) view the equatorial bond lengths look unevenly foreshortened and one equatorial Cl sits very close to the axial sphere, making the trigonal-bipyramidal arrangement slightly harder to read than in the source where the five directions are clearly distinct.

Panel (b)'s orbital lobes and green dashed trigonal-bipyramid framework are only reachable behind a toggle, so the sp3d lobe labels (the main annotation of the source figure) are not visible in the default state.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and pedagogically strong reconstruction of both panels with correct trigonal-bipyramidal geometry, teardrop sp3d lobes, dashed framework and genuinely useful toggles/tour/click-linking; main weaknesses are darker-than-source material colors and the loss of the side-by-side two-panel composition in the default view.
action_items: Brighten the materials/lighting so P and bonds match the source's saturated orange (#E8721C rendering true) and Cl matches the lighter green; reduce roughness or raise ambient light.
Consider defaulting to the 'Overlay both' or offering a true side-by-side layout (two groups offset in x with (a)/(b) captions) so the figure reads like the original two-panel image at first glance.
Even out the apparent equatorial bond lengths/spacing (or slightly rotate the default azimuth) so all five P–Cl directions are clearly separated as in the source.
Show a small static preview or thumbnail of panel (b) labels in the default view, or start the tour on step 2, so the 'sp3d' annotations — the key text of the source — are encountered immediately.

feedback.rationale: The concept and elements are correct; the fixes needed are implementation-level (material colors/lighting, default layout/camera, label visibility), not conceptual.

plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating sp3d hybridization in phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5) at the molecular and orbital levels. Panel (a) shows a ball-and-stick model of PCl5 with an orange phosphorus atom at the center covalently bonded to five green chlorine atoms directed toward the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid: two axial Cl atoms situated above and below the central P atom along a vertical axis, and three equatorial Cl atoms arranged symmetrically in the horizontal plane. Panel (b) depicts the five sp3d hybrid orbitals that account for these five bonds, each shown as a large orange lobe radiating from a central black dot representing the phosphorus nucleus, labeled "sp3d," and arranged in the same trigonal bipyramidal pattern with dashed lines connecting the lobe tips to outline the geometry; small back-lobes are omitted for clarity. This figure establishes sp3d hybridization — derived from mixing one 3s, three 3p, and one 3d orbital of phosphorus — as the valence-bond explanation for the five equivalent bonding regions in PCl5 and connects orbital theory directly to the observed trigonal bipyramidal molecular structure.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: P nucleus at origin; bond length 1.6 units to equatorial Cl and 1.8 units to axial Cl (axial bonds slightly longer, as in real PCl5). Directions: axial = (0,+1,0) and (0,−1,0); equatorial = unit vectors in the XZ plane at 0°, 120°, 240° (i.e. (1,0,0), (−0.5,0,0.866), (−0.5,0,−0.866)). Panel (a): P sphere radius 0.38, orange #E8721C with lighter specular highlight; Cl spheres radius 0.30, green #4CAF3E / #5CB85C; bond cylinders radius 0.09, orange #E8721C, spanning from P surface to Cl center. Panel (b): black nucleus dot radius 0.07 (#000000); each sp3d lobe is a teardrop/egg shape ~1.5 units long and ~0.55 units max width, fat end outward, narrow tip at the nucleus, axis aligned with its bond direction; fill light-orange gradient #F7C15C → #F0A63C with soft edges, semi-transparent (opacity ~0.85). Small back-lobes are omitted. Dashed lines: green #6E9B3A, 2px, dash 0.09/0.07, drawn as the 9 edges of the trigonal bipyramid connecting lobe-tip endpoints (3 equatorial-equatorial edges, 3 top-apex-to-equatorial, 3 bottom-apex-to-equatorial). Labels 'sp³d' in black italic serif, placed just beyond each lobe tip along its outward direction, offset ~0.35 units outward; panel captions '(a)' and '(b)' centered below each figure. Source view is roughly three-quarter: equatorial plane seen edge-on with a slight downward tilt so one equatorial direction points right, one upper-left, one lower-left; axial lobes read as top and bottom.
interactionPlan.notes: Build both panels as two THREE.Group objects sharing the same five direction vectors, so highlighting is index-linked. Lobes: generate a teardrop via LatheGeometry from a profile r(t) = A·sin(πt)·t^0.6 over t∈[0,1] (pinched at nucleus, bulging near tip), then orient with quaternion setFromUnitVectors(+Y, dir); use MeshStandardMaterial with slight transparency and an emissive tint for highlight state. Dashed geometry via LineSegments + LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Labels as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML so the sp³ superscript renders correctly and stays screen-facing during orbit. Click picking via Raycaster against lobe meshes and bond cylinders/Cl spheres; on select, set the matching lobe and the matching bond+Cl to a highlight color (e.g. #FFD24D lobe, #2E7D32 Cl) and dim the rest to ~0.25 opacity. In 'Overlay both' mode render panel (b) lobes translucent on top of the ball-and-stick model in the same coordinate frame rather than side by side. Toggle between (a) and (b) with a short cross-fade rather than an instant swap so the shared directions are visually preserved.
